reviewer_role: Independent of author; personally read all complete source units, target passages, categories, rationales, necessary context, two unresolved target proposals, and eight corrected complete triples.
review_method: Freshly read every complete source-target-category-rationale triple through show-triples.py/complete_text in the recorded unclipped batches. This personally covered all 120 actual source units and all 199 distinct retained target units. Separately read necessary contexts in 1 Chronicles 16:37-43, 17:1-15, 20:1-8, 23:12-20, 24:20-31, 26:20-28, 28:1-21, 29:1-23; 2 Samuel 12:26-31 and 21:15-22; 1 Kings 3:5-14, 5:15-32, 8:15-22; Exodus 18:1-6 and 28:1-4; Numbers 3:1-10 and 18:1-7; Leviticus 2:1-10 and 24:1-9; Joshua 1:1-9. Independently evaluated both unresolved proposals and their neighboring genealogy. Validated the six author corrections as an exact preserved before/after delta and personally reread each complete changed triple. Proposed two further wording corrections; personally read the corrected complete triples and confirmed the other 133 rows remained exact. No reading or semantic approval is inherited from the author.
same_chapter_review: All same-chapter links were personally checked for meaningful grammar, named family branches, numerical allocations, narrative causes or resolutions, or explicit governing list scope. The priestly names and ordinals in 24:7-18 fall under 24:5-6; the remaining-Levites entries fall within 24:20-31. These links establish the entries' stated roles and do not resolve identity by a similar name. No same-chapter label is missing or falsely applied.
precision_findings: Retained the distinct warriors, opponents, locations, name forms, agency descriptions, census totals, gold and silver sums, age thresholds, family headings, and priestly/Levitical roles. Preserved methachabin and araab without supplying meanings. 1 Kings 5:29-32 contains actual units 29, 30, and 32; no missing 31 was invented. Compared David's house and temple supplies only within the stated material connection. Required clearer wording for David's own confession and the Levites' comparative lot procedure; those two issues are resolved.
pin_method: Independently freshly fetched all seven complete used book files from the immutable raw GitHub commit into own peer-independent raw files. Checked each Git blob SHA1 against the fixed source-check registry, recorded raw SHA256, and compared every parsed book against the entire actual cache. Revalidated all seven saved raw SHA256/Git blobs and whole-cache equality at freeze. Did not reuse author raw downloads as peer fetch evidence.

unresolved_candidates.reason: Personally read Chebron's Idoud/Amadia/Oziel/Ikemias list and the Jediou list with Amadia/Jaziel/Jokom in second through fourth places. The shared Amadia and ordinal pattern do not independently establish the altered heading and other persons as identical. Retained 23:19 to 23:12 is supported by the explicit Chebron branch, regardless of this proposal.

Personally read Issari/Salomoth/Jath against Issaar's son Salomoth the ruler. Repeated Salomoth does not by itself prove the Issari/Issaar family equation; no such identity is credited. The retained 24:22 to 24:20-21 link independently locates the Issari entry under the remaining sons of Levi heading.

resolved_findings.resolution: David asks concerning his own wickedness as God's servant; the former rationale could instead make David's servant the offender.

old_row.relationship: Confession parallel: David admits foolishness after the census
old_row.rationale: David confesses great sin, asks removal of his servant's wickedness or lawlessness, and acknowledges extreme folly in both accounts. Samuel explicitly places the confession after David's heart struck him following the count.

new_row.relationship: Confession parallel: David admits foolishness after the census
new_row.rationale: David confesses great sin, asks God to take away his wickedness or lawlessness, and acknowledges extreme folly in both accounts. Samuel explicitly places the confession after David's heart struck him following the count.

resolved_findings.resolution: The source compares the Levites' lots with Aaron's sons using as did; alongside could imply a joint allocation that the source does not explicitly state.

old_row.relationship: Same-chapter roster purpose: Kis's son Iramael within Levitical allocation
old_row.rationale: The source adds Iramael as Kis's son. The following summary identifies the continuing list as Levites by ancestral houses who received lots alongside Aaron's sons, explaining the function of this otherwise brief family entry.

new_row.relationship: Same-chapter roster purpose: Kis's son Iramael within Levitical allocation
new_row.rationale: The source adds Iramael as Kis's son. The following summary identifies the continuing list as Levites by ancestral houses who also received lots, as Aaron's sons did, explaining the function of this otherwise brief family entry.

scope_limitations: Curated supplied-English semantic review only. Two unresolved target proposals receive zero completion credit; every source unit instead has an independently supported retained link.
